scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A query, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE is checked over the visit infos of the build that plans it (`table_privilege::check_plan_privilege`: a query's before it is optimized, a DML's once it is built, a point plan's through `check_fast_plan_privilege`). PREPARE and a new non-prepared plan-cache entry still collect their `VisitInfos` with the visit-only builds `query_visit_info` / `dml_visit_info` (`Session::collect_table_privileges`) and build their plans separately, where Go's `GeneratePlanCacheStmtWithAST` keeps those of its one `PlanBuilder.Build`; plain `EXPLAIN INSERT`, which plans no VALUES or ON DUPLICATE expressions (Go's `buildInsert` does), checks the visit-only pass's; and an INSERT's visit infos come from the separate builders of its target, source and values, where Go's `buildInsert` has one `PlanBuilder`

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: 53 of Go's 86 `ddl.executor` methods (`pkg/ddl/executor.go`) have no counterpart, `DoDDLJob` / `DoDDLJobWrapper` among them: a statement is lowered into this port's own `DdlStatement` (`cluster_ddl.rs` `lower_ddl_with_context`, then a `lower_*` builder) and submitted by `submit_built_job` / `submit_persisted_job_with_retry`; the missing methods include `AlterSchema`, `CreateTableWithInfo` / `BatchCreateTableWithInfo`, `RebaseAutoID`, `ShardRowID`, `ChangeColumn`, `RenameColumn`, `RenameIndex`, `DropView`, `CreatePrimaryKey`, `LockTables`, `CleanupTableLock`, `RepairTable`, `CreateSequence` / `AlterSequence`, the placement-policy, check-constraint, masking-policy, TTL, cache and attribute alters

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: No ingest (fast-reorg) backfill: it falls back to the transactional merge (`tidb-ddl/src/cluster_ddl/add_index.rs`); with it the status port's `/ingest/*` routes (Go `IngestConcurrencyHandler` over `ingestctrl`'s rate-limit parameters) are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: Cancellation follows Go's `convertJob2RollbackJob` for every action the worker runs. A columnar (vector, inverted, full-text) index is checked against its table as Go's `createColumnarIndex` does (`add_index.rs` `create_columnar_index`, `checkTableTypeForColumnarIndex`), but on a table with a columnar replica this node builds no `ActionAddColumnarIndex` job: `onCreateColumnarIndex` (TiFlash schema sync, `checkColumnarIndexProcess`) and its `rollingbackAddColumanrIndex` are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A multi-schema change has no `promoteProxyKVDiskFullPause`, whose only producer (`autoPauseAddIndexJobOnKVDiskFull`, the DXF add-index task) Rust lacks (D02, O10)

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A persisted DDL job step's action handlers take their objects from a catalog rebuilt from the whole step snapshot (`plan_persisted_ddl_job_with` -> `load_info_schema`, a `TableInfo` JSON parse per table, system tables included), where Go's handlers read the job's own objects through `jobCtx.metaMut` (`checkSchemaExistAndCancelNotExistJob`, `GetTableInfoAndCancelFaultJob`) and take only the schema-version context from `jobCtx.infoCache`. The rebuilt catalog is raw meta, not an `InfoSchema`: a DROP DATABASE's later steps still find the write-only database there, while Go's infoschema drops it at the first diff (`applyDropSchema`), so the cached schema cannot stand in until the handlers read meta. In the `executor/foreign_key` and `ddl/db_integration` replays about half of every DDL's latency is that rebuild

Root HashAgg is Go's `HashAggExec` (`tidb-executor-aggregate/src/agg_hash_executor.rs`: fetcher, partial workers shuffling one mapper per final worker, final workers, `parallelHashAggSpillHelper` spill), and its serial and parallel memory are Go's to the byte for global and pushed-down aggregates (`sum(a)` 12.6 KB, `b, count(a) ... group by b` 13.5 KB, `count(distinct b)` 12.4 KB) except a grouped scan-fed one (`a, group_concat(b) ... group by a` 14.0 KB where a fresh Go session's holds 14.8 KB) and an index-fed `count(distinct a)` (12.3 KB / 12.6 KB), for a reason not yet found (Go's `groupKeyPool` / `partialResultsBufferPool` recycle buffers across statements, so a later statement in one Go session charges more); a cop-side partial aggregation run in this tier (trailing group-key columns, `Partial1`/`Partial2` modes) still runs the old `AggState` engine (`lib.rs` `HashAggExec` / `GroupedStreamAggExec`, `parallel.rs`)

`IndexLookUpExecutor`'s memory and RU v2 are Go's, on every run: the double read (`IndexRangeSourceExec`, `access_path.rs` `IndexLookUpMemory`) owns a tracker labelled with its plan that each open attaches to the statement's, charged with its index ranges' KV ranges (`buildTableKeyRanges`), the index worker's responses (`LabelForIndexWorker`) and each table task's `executeTask` bytes (`cap(handles)` and the handles, the task's `TableReaderExecutor` at 768 plus its KV ranges and `dagPB.Size()`, the chunks it fills, `task.rows`, a keep-order `indexOrder` and `rowIdx`), the next task releasing the last; each task's reader records `TableReaderExecutor` into the parent's accumulator. EXPLAIN ANALYZE and `tidb_mem_quota_query` match Go for integer, keep-order `_tidb_rowid` and clustered handles (`tests_explain.rs` `an_index_lookup_charges_its_tasks_like_go`). Remaining: an unordered lookup whose output lacks the handle appends it to the table request to associate rows (`SELECT c FROM t USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 1`, or `SELECT *` over a `_tidb_rowid` table), so its DAG and chunks are a column wider than Go's (2.54 KB where Go shows 2.14 KB); a task (one `next_lookup_batch` window) is cut at the batch size where Go's `extractTaskHandles` keeps the whole chunk `readFromChunk` hands it (`ReuseIntermChk`), so a small batch splits Go's one task (6 rows at `tidb_index_lookup_size` 2: Go one 2.58 KB task, this port three, 4.92 KB), and a window spans the partitions Go gives a task each (`p ... PARTITION BY HASH(a) PARTITIONS 2`, `b > 1`: Go two tasks, 5.13 KB, this port one, 4.29 KB); a task the store answers without a table reader (`LookupFetch::LocalFallback`: a dirty transaction's read, a refused remote shape) charges nothing; a `LocalIndexLookUp`'s index-side responses hold handles where Go's hold the completed rows; and the reader is one source shared with `IndexReader` and index-merge partials, its tasks windows of one `LookupPipeline` over a `LanePool`, not Go's index worker, table workers and `resultCh`

`IndexJoin` and `IndexHashJoin` are Go's `IndexLookUpJoin` and `IndexNestedLoopHashJoin` (`join/index_lookup_join.rs`, `join/index_lookup_hash_join.rs`: outer and inner workers over `Joiner`), with Go's task memory and matching; the fused `JoinExec` lookup strategy is gone. Two gaps remain: Go's `IndexLookUpMergeJoin` executor (and `PhysicalIndexMergeJoin`'s `KeyOff2KeyOffOrderByIdx`, `CompareFuncs`, `NeedOuterSort`, `Desc`) is unported -- neither planner builds one on this branch, and the builder refuses the kind; and Go's `IndexJoinExecutorBuilder` builds each task's inner executor afresh, where this port's inner workers re-seed one shared `IndexLookupSource` under a lock unless the lookup forks (a common-handle prefix)

The embedded store's coprocessor runs every DAG through Go's `mppExec` chain (`tidb-unistore-cophandler` `mpp.rs`, `mpp_exec.rs`), but `selExec` filters row by row where Go's `expression.VectorizedFilter` evaluates each condition over the whole chunk, the index-lookup push-down (`buildIndexLookUp` and its intermediate outputs) refuses, and a store or row-decode error answers `OtherError` where `genRespWithMPPExec` carries it in `SelectResponse.error`

A TiKV reader builds its DAG from its access path's scan request (`cop_reader.rs`; `cop_plan_ids_for` matches executors to the pushed nodes by kind) where Go's `constructDAGReq` lowers the reader's pushed plan one node per executor (`ToPB`). A reader's TopN reaches the coprocessor only through the scan's `accept_remote_topn` offer, so a TopN over an expression stays local (`PushdownTopNOrder` carries a column offset, where `PhysicalTopN.ToPB` lowers any `ByItem`), and an IndexLookUp's index-side TopN (`TopN_19(Build)`) is never offered (`accept_index_top_n` has no caller): its lookup reads every matching handle where Go's reads only the TopN's

A projection's vectorized result column takes the shape its Go builtin's `vecEval*` gives it (`chunk_executor.rs`: `Resize*`, `Reserve*` and appends, one argument evaluated into it, a column's `CopyReconstruct`) for arithmetic, comparisons and `IN`, logic, `NOT`/`IS NULL`/`IS TRUE`, casts, `IF`/`IFNULL`/`CASE`/`COALESCE`, and the math, time-field and common string builtins; a tree holding any other builtin (JSON functions, `GREATEST`/`LEAST` over strings, `LOCATE`, `ADDTIME`/`SUBTIME`, `CONVERT_TZ`, `ANY_VALUE`, user-variable and info functions, ...) still appends row by row, so `SELECT greatest(c, 'x'), a+1` over 100 rows peaks at 12.1 KB where Go's is 12.4 KB (12693 B) and `SELECT locate('s', c), a+1` at 10.6 KB where Go's is 10.5 KB (10778 B). The values still come from the row and batch evaluators rather than Go's `vecEval*` kernels, and `IF`'s row fallback when its condition warns (`fallbackEval*`, which resizes) is not modelled

The session's reusable chunk allocator is Go's (`Session::chunk_alloc`, Go `clientConn.chunkAlloc`: installed per statement as `NewSyncAllocator(alloc)` under `tidb_enable_reuse_chunk`, never for an internal `InRestrictedSQL` statement, reset between statements and recreated after a failed one, each statement's validity its own), executors take it as `ExecutorMeta::alloc_pool` (Go `AllocPool`) for `NewChunk` / `TryNewCacheChunk` / `NewChunkWithCapacity`, and Go's `NewFirstChunk` sites (`Executor::new_first_chunk`: projection workers, hash-join probe and result chunks, index-hash-join results, shuffle holders, the drained record set) allocate outside it, so memory charges match Go's in sequence (`a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`, `explain_analyze_dml_roots_report_their_executor_stats_and_memory_like_go`). Remaining: executors built outside the physical builder's `meta` (`ExecutorMeta::new` in other crates) allocate fresh; parallel apply's chunks, whose executor shape differs from Go's, are unmapped; the reuse hook's `StmtCtx.SetUseChunkAlloc` (`@@last_sql_use_alloc`) is not driven by allocation

The session tracker's `LabelForMemDB` child follows the transaction buffer's PAYLOAD (key, value and value-history bytes, kept incrementally in the client's `Art` / `Rbt`) and its hook fires on every write, where client-go's `MemDB.Mem()` is its arenas' CAPACITY (`arena.go` blocks doubling from 4 KB to 128 MB) and its hook fires only when an arena enlarges (`onMemChange`); the session-side hook, its detach in `ActivateTxn` and the non-default `TxnTotalSizeLimit` skip are Go's

An Apply whose inner side holds a CTE correlated to the Apply's outer row runs serially (`cte_correlated_to` in `driver/physical_builder.rs`), where Go runs it on the parallel workers: Go's workers share the one CTE producer `buildApply` builds from the original inner plan (`CTEStorageMap`), whose correlated cells no worker binds, so Go answers every such row NULL (gorun: `SELECT a, (WITH c AS (SELECT t2.a FROM t t2 WHERE t2.a <= t.a) SELECT SUM(x.a) FROM c x JOIN c y ON x.a = y.a) FROM t` gives NULL on every row under `tidb_enable_parallel_apply`, 1, 3, 6, ... serially). This port keeps the correct serial answer; an uncorrelated CTE shares its producer across the workers as Go's does
IMPORT INTO refuses (`tidb-session/src/dispatch.rs`)

`ReportMinStartTS` has no InfoCache recent-schema TS (`GetAndResetRecentInfoSchemaTS`, InfoSchema V2: I04). Lazy cursor fetch answers Go's `executor.Detach` over the physical plan (`tidb_executor::detach`), because the builder's operator tree is not Go's executor tree; `buildTableReader`'s `TableDualExec` for an empty pruned partition set is not modeled there. A detached statement still publishes its completion through its record set's close, where Go never runs the abandoned `recordSet`'s `CloseRecordSet`

No cross-keyspace runtime (null keyspace only); the next-gen-only surfaces built on it have no port either: the status port's `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*`, and plan replayer's `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` storage (`pkg/planner/extstore` `createGlobalExtStorage`, local files on a classic kernel)

The MPP coordinator lowers a hand-built single-fragment scan DAG and refuses every pushed Selection, TopN and aggregation, where Go builds the fragment/task graph from the physical plan (including disaggregated compute placement)

`pkg/executor/mppcoordmanager` (`MPPCoordinatorManager`: coordinator registration, `detectAndDelete` expiry, the server address) and the RPC server's `ReportMPPTaskStatus` have no port, so TiFlash's task-status reports reach no coordinator; Go's coordinator only asks TiFlash for reports when its plan has a Limit above the table reader (`needReportExecutionSummary`), which the single-fragment scan never builds (M01)

PD's `serviceDiscovery` (`servicediscovery/service_discovery.go`) is not one owner here: member updates and the leader connection live in `pd/cluster.rs` / `pd/retry.rs`, with no per-member `serviceClient`, no `apiCandidateNodes` / `GetServiceClientByKind` (how Go picks a follower for a follower-handled region API) and no `checkServiceModeChanged`
No Cascades memo exploration/implementation in the production optimizer

SQL/PB signature construction and typed vector execution. The planner's `BuiltinFunctionUsageInc` (`expressionRewriter.newFunction`) is not called: it needs the function's `PbCode`, which a planner-built Rust function only gets at pushdown resolution.
No lazy InfoSchema V2, schema-cache-size loader/evictor or InfoCache timestamp ranges

A CLUSTER_* table's TiDB-store reader sends Go's DAG (`builder_utils.rs`: `ConstructDAGReq`'s list-form `ToPB`, `SetHandleRanges`) and every TiDB rebuilds it with `coprocessor.rs`'s `PBPlanBuilder`; still apart from Go: `TIFLASH_REPLICA`'s TiDB-store reader runs its pushed plan as local executors where Go sends it to the DDL owner (`GetClusterTableCopDestination`, `SetTiDBServerID`); `SqlDigestTextRetriever`'s global pass hand-builds a TableScan plus DIGEST IN request (`ClusterPeerClient::scan_projected` via `peer_cluster_table_rows`) where Go's `RetrieveGlobal` runs `ExecRestrictedSQL` over CLUSTER_STATEMENTS_SUMMARY(_HISTORY); the reader records no cop runtime statistics from the responses (Go `selectResult.updateCopRuntimeStats`), so EXPLAIN ANALYZE's TableReader row lacks `cop_task`/`rpc_info` and its cop[tidb] rows show `N/A` where Go shows 0 rows; the requester answers its own task with its coprocessor handler in-process instead of over its status port; `StatementsSummaryExtractor.CoarseTimeRange` does not reach the v2 summary reader (Go `buildTimeRanges`)
BRIE statements are classified but never executed
No DXF scheduler/executor managers composed

TopSQL is ported over pprof-rs (`tidb-cpuprofile`, `tidb-topsql-collector`, `tidb-topsql-reporter`, `tidb-topsql`): the status port serves `TopSQLPubSub`, the single-target sink reports to `top-sql.receiver-address`, each command labels its thread `{connID}_{sqlID}`, each statement registers its SQL and plan and labels the thread with both digests, and the profiler's TiDB CPU reaches PROCESSLIST and the statement summary. The DDL worker attaches each job step and each backfill task to the job's SQL (`tidb-ddl` `job_ctx.rs`, Go `ReorgContext.attachTopProfilingInfo`). The step's transaction carries the job's resource-group tagger (`getResourceGroupTaggerForTopSQL`, published into its statement kv context once the step loads the job). Unported: the DXF backfill executor's attach (O10) and the fast-reorg skip checks' (`checkIfTableReorgWorkCanSkip` / `checkIfTempIndexReorgWorkCanSkip`, D02), and the multi-statement prefetch's plan hand-off: `prefetchPointPlanKeys` reads (or locks) the point writes' keys before the statements run (`cluster_session_node/prefetch.rs`, with its `setResourceGroupTaggerForMultiStmtPrefetch`), but its point plans are not handed to the statements (Go `PointPlanKey`), which plan again. Executors register the statement's SQL and plan on their first `Next` with Top profiling on (`RegisterSQLAndPlanInExecForTopProfiling`, `SqlKillerCheckExec`); profiler labels follow Go's goroutine inheritance (`labels::inherit`) into the shuffle, hash-join build, checksum, coprocessor, slow-log parse, cluster-table fan-out, analyze and global-stats merge, DDL analyze workers and the MPP client's store probes

The DDL scheduler, systable manager, history and MDL readers scan records instead of running SQL on `DdlSessionPool::sess_pool`; the bootstrap stages raw rows; accounts load eagerly where Go loads per active user
